elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits termination "by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" with no cause requirement, so the Company has a no-cause exit; the Order Form limb is inapplicable because this hosting agreement has no Order Forms. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a keyword miss (no express "for convenience" wording), not an absence of a no-cause right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered still requires "ninety (90) days written notice"; the redline did not touch the notice period.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation appears anywhere in the rendered text; the money flows the other way \u2014 revised 4.2(a) requires "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment". Nothing was added to require HDI to refund prepaid amounts.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 gives HDI the identical 90-day no-cause right, and the following sentence \u2014 "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" \u2014 lets the terminating party pick any date at least 90 days out, so it is not clear on the face of the text that HDI's right is confined to the renewal date rather than exercisable mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 (unchanged): "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other". The Company therefore has a no-cause exit on exactly 90 days' notice, at the outer edge of the 60\u201390 day window, and on either reading of the clause (mid-term or anniversary-only) that exit is available at least annually in a one-year term.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Revised 4.2(a): the Termination Payment "shall be an amount equal to, and shall in no event exceed, the aggregate payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date". Section 3.1 payments are the fees, so the exit charge is expressly ceilinged at three months' fees; the favourable eight-quarter instalment mechanic in (c) survives.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The operative text is symmetric \u2014 "terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" \u2014 and contains no words limiting HDI's exercise to the expiry of the then-current term. The drafter reads the same sentence as an at-will right for the Company but an anniversary-only right for HDI; the words do not support that asymmetry, and the "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence permits any Termination Date 90+ days out. Repair: add to Section 4.1, e.g., "provided that HDI may terminate under this Section 4.1 only effective as of the expiration of the then-current one (1) year term."

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires "ninety (90) days written notice" from either Party, so HDI cannot exit on shorter notice; this also keeps the clause out of walk-away territory.

reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the original 4.2(a) exit charge (aggregate trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000, halved \u2014 roughly $600,000 on $2,000,000 of Net Sales against about $140,000 of three months' fees), imposed on the Company alone with no reciprocal HDI payment (p0028), materially fails the fallback cap. This is not a mere sub-element shortfall and is properly redlined.

Fallback is not position-complete: element 3 ("Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term") is left to interpretation of untouched symmetric language. Add express operative words to Section 4.1 limiting HDI's Section 4.1 termination to take effect only at the expiration of the then-current one-year term (the Company's right can remain exercisable on 90 days' notice at any time). Do not rest the position on the margin comment's assertion that HDI's right "operates only to stop renewal at an anniversary" \u2014 the words do not say that.

Minimality defect: the redline replaces the whole formula instead of capping it, discarding customer-favourable existing language. Under the original clause no Termination Payment was due where trailing twelve-month Net Sales were $800,000 or less; under the revision the Company always owes three months of Section 3.1 fees (about $50,000 at $800,000 of Net Sales, where it previously owed nothing), and the revision only improves the Company's position above roughly $871,000 of trailing Net Sales. Redraft as a ceiling on the existing calculation, e.g. "an amount equal to the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the aggregate payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date".

Vestigial text: the retained paragraph (b) ("Payment is determined pursuant to this Section 4.2 to be less than or equal to zero...") was drafted for the netting formula and is now near-inoperative, since a three-month fee measure cannot be negative. It does not contradict the new sentence, so intent is preserved, but the drafter should confirm it is not read as implying a netting/offset mechanic that no longer exists.

Residual point to raise in the comment (optional, outside the fallback checklist): 4.2(a) still bites on "the event the Company terminates this Agreement" generally, including a termination for HDI's breach. If the counterparty resists a carve-out, note it rather than adding scope beyond the checklist \u2014 but a short proviso ("other than a termination by the Company arising from HDI's breach") would align with Section 1.6's "without penalty" concept.

Preferred level is not attempted and correctly so on this record: 30-day notice and a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund are absent, and the fee model (percentage of Net Sales) makes a refund mechanic an awkward fit. Tone, prefix and length of the margin comment comply with the playbook, subject to removing the unsupported asymmetric reading of Section 4.1.
